evidence: Class is now certain: the neighbours Field_HorseAction_Ctor (0x0036C54C), Field_HorseAction_DeletingDtor and Field_HorseAction_UpdateMotion are confirmed names, so the Field_HorseAction prefix is right. name: Field_HorseAction_Update

params.dt: frame delta time, passed in s0 and forwarded to Actor_UpdateTurnBlend

evidence: Disassembly shows the real signature is (self, float dt): s0 is saved to s16, restored before Actor_UpdateTurnBlend and before the epilogue. The body is the same skeleton as the base action update 0x0036D2E8 plus one extra branch, and that branch is byte-for-byte the mounted branch of the already-named Field_HorseAction_Start (0x0036C314): same actor+0x2d4 mounted flag, same Sound_Emitter_PlayStepSe(actor,1), same actor+0x276 = 1. Class confirmed by Field_HorseAction_Ctor/DeletingDtor/UpdateMotion.

evidence: Corrected: the old name called it an Actor method, but self is the ACTION (vtable at +0, actor at +0x28) and the body is exactly the action-update skeleton that the confirmed Field_HorseAction_Update (0x0036C440) overrides - same three helpers, same vtable+0x34 motion-id query, same actor+0x290 clear, and 0x0036C440 even tail-jumps into this function's shared epilogue at 0x0036D350. name: maybe_Ui_CompareRow_SetValueFromByte

params.self: row object; the target pane is at +0x22c
params.memberIdPtr: pointer to one byte holding the party member index

summary: Sets a row's value to a party member's remaining amount: resolves the member record from the byte at memberIdPtr, computes (u16 at member+0x12dc) - (u16 at member+0xe6) clamped at 0, and stores it on the pane at self+0x22c.
evidence: Disassembly of the split symbol 0x00629280 pins the arithmetic exactly: ldrh r1,[r0,#0xe6]; ldrh r0,[r2,r0] with r2 = 0x12dc (pc-relative literal 0x000012DC), so it is *(u16*)(member+0x12dc) - *(u16*)(member+0xe6), clamped to 0 and zero-extended. That is a remaining/available value, which is why the row is fed a computed number rather than a raw record field. What the +0x12dc limit and the +0xe6 counter actually are is still unknown, and 'CompareRow' is only the shape of the caller's pane, so maybe_ stays.

name: Casino_Slot_PlaceBet

summary: Places the current slot-machine bet: turns the payout rank (0/1/2) into the 1x/10x/100x stake multiplier, subtracts multiplier x bet from the casino coin counter at work+0x31f4 (capped at 9,999,999, dirty bit set at work+0x5be0) and refreshes the coin display pane at record[0xc]+0x128.

The delta is negated, so the bet is deducted. The multiplier comes from the already-named Casino_Slot_GetPayoutRank and the read-back 0x0066B2CC(work+0x24a98,0) returns the same +0x31f4 counter, which is then shown via 0x00405D90.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_ChooseMessage

params.self: battle member widget; +0x50 actor, +0x50+0x12d8 message context, +0xd2 busy flag

summary: Decides whether the member gets a battle message this step and queues it: checks the actor's state and the message context, resolves the message row with Battle_Message_ResolveRowOffset, sets the busy flag at +0xd2 and queues either action 0x552 or the balloon id 0x23/0x24 through Battle_QueueActionEx; returns 1 when something was queued.
evidence: Both callees are named - Battle_QueueActionEx (0x001F8534) and Battle_Message_ResolveRowOffset (0x00485D90) - so 'queue a battle message for this member' is solid, and the two balloon ids 0x23/0x24 are chosen from the context byte at +0xb0f7. The 'MemberWidget' class and the 'slot 12' role are still inherited from the vtable family, and 'Choose' is an interpretation of the guard, so maybe_ stays.

name: Battle_TargetMarker_AssignSlots

params.self: marker list; 26 entries of 8 bytes, +0xd0 target actor, +0xd4 used flag

summary: Gives every target marker its own target: for each marker it scans the 26 slots for a free one (+0xd0 set, +0xd4 clear), builds a row for the candidate actor with Text_BuildRowForActor and keeps the slot with the smallest vtable+0x90 metric, marks it used and moves on; returns 1 when all markers were served, 0 when the marker list runs out first.
evidence: The caller is the named Battle_TargetMarker_Update (0x003D0B68) and the callee is the named Text_BuildRowForActor (0x00490994), so both the 'target marker' owner and the row-building step are fixed. The body is two 26-entry loops with the +0xd0/+0xd4 free-slot test and the vtable+0x90 comparison, exactly as the summary says.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnPageSelect

params.self: dive form; +0x3770 flag word, +0x3d4 page selector, +0x984 page entry list, +0x134 pane stack

summary: Handles a page-selection notification on the dive form: with flag bit 4 it pops the pane, with bit 0x142 it reads the selected page and - unless the page is the 'none' sentinel 9 - rebuilds the page entries, releases the row tweens and commits through 0x0029126C, and with bit 1 it forwards the three bytes at +0x3772..+0x3774 to 0x001A60A0.
evidence: The DiveForm owner is confirmed by the named callees Ui_DiveForm_BuildPageEntries, Ui_DiveForm_PopPane, Ui_DiveForm_PushPane and maybe_Ui_DiveForm_ReleaseRowTweens, and the page read plus the sentinel 9 support the 'page select' reading. What is not proven is the trigger: the function is a flag-driven dispatcher with three independent branches and both page branches end in the non-returning 0x0029126C, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_TalkBalloon_Dtor

params.self: object; embedded Ui_Object at +0x00, sprite at +0x64
params.vtable: vtable pointer stamped into the object before teardown

summary: Deleting destructor of a small object that owns one sprite at +0x64 and one embedded Ui_Object at +0: stamps the passed vtable, destroys the sprite with Gfx_Sprite_DtorAlt, destroys the Ui_Object body and frees the instance.
evidence: The teardown shape is certain (stamp vtable, Gfx_Sprite_DtorAlt(self+0x64), Ui_Object_DtorBody(self), free via 0x0010F6CC) and both callees are named. The class is not: there is no caller and no data table points here, and the same three-step body appears at several addresses with only the sprite offset changed, so 'TalkBalloon' stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_Dtor_D7714

params.self: object; embedded Ui_Object at +0x00, sprite at +0x4c
params.vtable: vtable pointer stamped into the object before teardown

name: maybe_Field_Actor_DeleteSubObjects

params.actor: large actor object; two sprites and three Ui_Object bodies below +0x37c
params.vtable: vtable pointer stamped into the object before teardown

The class is still a layout inference (the address is in no data table) and the name Field_Actor_DeletingDtor is already taken by 0x003A4F48, so the existing name is kept with the destructor role spelled out in the summary.

name: maybe_Battle_SetUnitModelVariant
signature: void maybe_Battle_SetUnitModelVariant(BattleUnit* self, u32 setId, int index, u8* colors, u32 stored)

params.self: unit; +0x69 set id, +0x6a variant index, +0x6b last-variant flag, +0x6c..+0x6e colour overrides
params.setId: model-set id resolved through the data manager

summary: Applies one variant of a battle model set: resolves the set through Game_GetDataManager and 0x0063f108, takes the u16 model id at the requested index from the set's table, runs Battle_SetupUnitModelParts on it, copies the three colour overrides and records the set id, the variant index and whether this was the last variant.
evidence: Both principal callees are named (Game_GetDataManager, Battle_SetupUnitModelParts) and the body stores setId/index/last-flag/three colours, so the model-variant reading holds. The 20 reported callers are all field/scene functions, but spot-checking shows they do not actually branch to this address (0x0044B8AC and 0x003DA0C8 contain no reference to 0x003DB0A4), so they are split-symbol artifacts and do not contradict the Battle/Unit owner - which is still inherited rather than proven, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_BuildPartTable

params.self: message window; +0x158 part records (0xa8 bytes), +0x15c part count, +0x178 entry table (0x18 bytes), +0xa78 entry count

summary: Builds the drawable part entries for a message command: for every part whose animation state is 3 it writes a 0x18-byte entry (pane state, part record, colour pair, alpha defaults 0x1e/0x2a) and then adds the six sub-parts with flags 0x10/0x20/1/2/4/8.
evidence: The caller is the named Ui_MessagePage_ExecuteCommand and the callees are named (Ui_Part_GetAnimState, Ui_MessageWindow_ClampTextPosition), and the 0x18-byte entry stride and the six sub-part flags are readable. The body is still damaged - it ends in halt_baddata and the two alpha defaults arrive in lost registers (unaff_r10/unaff_r11) - so per FACTS.md it stays maybe_ below 0.5.

name: Field_Npc_ApplyModelVariant
signature: void Field_Npc_ApplyModelVariant(FieldNpc* self, int forwarded, int arg3, int arg4)

params.self: NPC object; +0x43 override flag, +0x22c party member index
params.forwarded: forwarded untouched to the variant setter 0x005E7848

summary: Picks the NPC's model variant: variant 3 when the override flag at +0x43 is set, otherwise variant 2 when the party member at +0x22c has bit 0x10 of +0xda set, else variant 1; the choice is applied through 0x005E7848.
evidence: The confirmed sibling Field_Actor_ApplyModelVariant (0x003E7660, no maybe_) has the identical body with only the id field changed (+0x200 vs +0x22c), and the caller is the named Field_Npc_UpdateModelFromTable - the NPC twin pattern. The three-way 1/2/3 choice is exactly what the sibling's confirmed name calls a model variant.

name: Model_Equip_GetBoneTransformDescriptor
signature: int Model_Equip_GetBoneTransformDescriptor(void* modelEquip, u32 equipCategory, int index, u32 unused)

params.index: sub-index for the multi-slot categories (6 and the default arm)

summary: Returns the bone-transform descriptor for one equipment category: resolves the CharacterRecord through the data manager and 0x0063eb94, then returns the per-category sub-record (0x160/0x1b0 for category 0, 0x200, 0x250, 0x2a0, 0x2f0, 0x340, 0x368+index*0x28, 0x3b8, 0x3e0, 0x408) that holds the bone name and Euler angles the item model is attached with.
evidence: Corrected: the old name put this in the UI text-label subsystem, but FACTS.md and the caller both place it in Model_Equip - the only caller is the confident Model_Equip_AttachItemSlot (0x0040B7A8, 0.72), which calls it as 0x0040AC1C(modelEquip, itemRec->u8_29) and then builds a 3x4 matrix from the returned Euler angles, defaulting to bone "N_ALL". The body matches: it resolves the CharacterRecord with 0x0063EB94(dm, self->f_65) and returns record + a per-equip-category offset.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DispatchToChildPane
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_DispatchToChildPane(UiWindow* self, u32* slot, LayoutElement* child, u32 value)

params.self: window; +0x10 attached pane object
params.slot: value slot; the word at +0x10 is forwarded
params.child: layout element; +0x60c is temporarily set to the slot

summary: Forwards a value to a layout element when the attached pane is visible (bit 0 of f_44) and resolves to a material: publishes the slot at child+0x60c, calls 0x0053cd1c with the slot value, writes the result back and clears the publication.
evidence: The caller is the confident Ui_Window_UpdateChildren and the callees are named (Gfx_SpritePane_GetPrimaryMaterial, and 0x0053CD1C which is a split symbol inside Ui_LayoutText_BuildBlockLayoutQuads), so 'forward a value into the layout' is solid. 'Child pane' is still an interpretation of the f_44 visibility test, and the target is a layout-text quad builder rather than a pane, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite_UpdateOrientationFromLayout

params.sprite: sprite; +0x99 packed s16 angle pair, +0x3c/+0x40 material sizes, +0x1c/+0x20/+0x24 computed transform, +0x44 flags

summary: Recomputes a sprite's orientation: reads two packed 16-bit values from the linked material through 0x0065dbc8, converts the s16 angle pair in f_99 to floats, writes the angle, the height offset (value - 128.0f) * 0.5f and 0 into f_1c/f_20/f_24, and sets the transform-dirty bit 0x10 of f_44.
evidence: The caller is the confident Ui_MonsterBook_InitData and the maths is now readable: f_1c = (float)(s16)f_99, f_20 = (float)(s16)(f_99>>16) + (u16 - 128.0f) * 0.5f, f_24 = 0, then bit 0x10 of f_44 is set. The values come from the material (0x0065DBC8), not from a layout record, so the 'FromLayout' wording is still loose and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_TextWindow_LoadEffect

The only caller, Ui_MonsterBook_InitData, does not settle whether 'effect' means a visual effect or a pane group, so maybe_ stays at 0.35.

name: maybe_Ui_SetBusyFlagAndLeave
